name: Mythic Machines
lines: An eight-legged walking fortress of brass, iron and steam, built long ago by a frontier engineer who meant to rule the plains with it. A boiler roars in its belly; a cannon deck rides on its back.
A page torn from an engineer's daybook, red with dust:

“I walked her into the shadow of the great mountain, where two red walls lean together and the wind cannot find her. Eight feet, all folded. When the sun sets behind the mountain, walk toward it and look where the cliffs close.”
The Engineer's Cabin
The Corsair Kestrel
twin turret lasers
Scratched into a frost-rimed cargo tag:
“Parked her where the ice cliffs sweat and the heart of Pluto turns to blue glass, far out past the landing lights. Charon watches the cave mouth. Bring a light and don't tell the Port Authority.”
The Twinvane Shrike
A one-seat fighter: a teardrop cockpit pod between two tall ribbed vanes that drink the sunlight, twin cannons under the chin, and an ion engine that hums rather than roars.
A flight log on a scratched data slate:
“Took a hit over the Sea of Tranquillity and put her down in the dark side of a crater rim, south-west of the old landing site, where the Earth can't see her. The vanes are still warm.”
The Avionics Crawlway
Ashvaal, the Pearl Domeship
A Veyari domeship: a great pearl dome riding on a slender hull, a long tapering tail with three fins, and violet light running in its ribs. Inside the dome is a garden of glowing crystal.
Words in Veyari glass-script, translated on the back by a careful hand:
“Ashvaal sleeps where the rose sun sets behind the singing spires, in the grove of tall crystal. Speak softly. The dome remembers its pilots.”
The Pilot's Cradle
The Tail Lance Gallery
The Ironhide Bulwark
A heavy tank with twin cannons in a turret the size of a cottage, tracks taller than a man, and armour a hand thick. The dwarves who sealed it away said it was too strong to be used.
Chalked on a mine-cart, in dwarvish runes and common letters:
“THE IRON BEAST IS WALLED UP WHERE THE OLD RAILS END, PAST THE DEEP WATER, IN THE CAVE THAT ECHOES TWICE. DO NOT WAKE IT.”
The Commander's Cupola
Rosehorn, the Pink Unicorn
right arm and sword
A unicorn of rose-pink armour with a silver mane and a long spiral horn. In the Mythic Sovereign it is the right arm, and its horn becomes the great sword.
A ribbon tied to a branch, with a note in a child's careful writing:
“The pink horse sleeps behind the tallest waterfall. You have to go through the water. I saw its horn glowing. Second star, then left, then a long way.”
Nightwyrm, the Black Dragon
left arm and shield
A black dragon of plated night-steel with violet light in its throat. In the Mythic Sovereign it is the left arm, and its folded wings become the great shield.
A scorched brass plate, still warm:
“Where the fog is thickest and the ground breaks into black glass, the wyrm coils inside the hollow hill. Go toward the brightest lightning. Its eyes glow violet in the murk.”
Emberwing, the Red Phoenix
wings, helmet and artillery
A phoenix of red and gold armour whose feathers glow like embers. In the Mythic Sovereign its wings become the Sovereign's wings, its crest the helmet, and its tail the shoulder cannons.
Letters burnt into a black stone:
“The firebird sleeps on the cold side of the great rim, where the Sun never looks, under a spire of rock shaped like a flame. Walk away from the Sun until your shadow is longest.”
Frostfang, the Blue Dire Wolf
A great dire wolf of ice-blue armour with white steel fangs. In the Mythic Sovereign it is the right leg.
A paw print pressed into a sheet of blue ice, and beside it, carved:
“Where the pines end and the snow goes on, the wolf keeps its den under the ridge that howls. Follow the north wind until it stops.”
Riddlecrown, the Purple Sphinx
A sphinx of violet and gold armour, a lion's body and wings folded on its back, a calm face that asks questions. In the Mythic Sovereign it is the left leg.
A message in a stoppered bottle, washed up on the sand:
“On the island no chart names, past the last of the others, a violet sphinx lies with its paws in the sea. It answers only those who come by boat.”
The Hall of Questions
Blazehorn, the Orange Minotaur
A towering minotaur of orange and iron armour, horns like two scimitars. In the Mythic Sovereign it is the body and the head, and its pilot leads.
A ball of red thread, with a tag:
“In the hedge maze nobody tends, at the far edge of the farms, the bull stands in the middle. Keep your right hand on the hedge and you will reach it.”
The Mythic Sovereign
artillery and the great sword
The Sovereign's Bridge
The Heart of the Six
An island no chart names
Past the last island on any chart
No chart names it. The sand is fine and violet-grey, and the wind seems to ask you something.
At its heart, among broken columns, a great shape lies with its paws stretched toward the sea.
nobody tends it now
a seam in the red rock
A seam runs through the rock here, far too straight to be natural. Sand has been brushed away from its foot, not long ago.
Stone grinds on stone. The ground at the heart of the canyon splits, and something vast unfolds up out of the dark.
something dark under the ice
Under the ice of the floor there is something dark and straight-edged, like the top of a hatch.
The ice cracks in a long ring. A hatch the size of a field swings down, and a ship rises slowly out of the deep cold.
a stone that sounds hollow
Tap this stone and it rings hollow. The dust around it is pressed flat in a ring, as if something heavy once sat here.
Under the stone is a handle. You pull, the crater floor slides apart, and a ship is lifted up into the starlight.
a crystal that hums
One crystal here hums when you come close. There is a hand-shaped hollow worn into it.
Lay your hand on it
The hum rises into one clear note. The grove floor opens like a flower, and a pearl-white dome rises out of it.
one stone colder than the rest
One stone in the back wall is colder than the others, and there is a thumb-sized hollow worn into its edge.
Chains rattle somewhere below. The vault floor drops away into a lift, and the iron beast comes grinding up out of the deep.
moss over a carved ring
Behind the water, moss has grown over a ring carved into the rock. Under the moss the stone is smooth, as if many hands have touched it.
Clear the moss and touch the ring
The ring glows faintly. The pool behind the falls drains away, and something pink and shining rises slowly out of the water.
a column with a crack in it
One black column has a crack running through it, and warm air breathes out of the crack.
Put your shoulder to it
The column swings aside. The hollow floor breaks open, and a great black shape uncoils up out of the dark.
ground that sounds hollow
Your footsteps sound hollow here. Under the dust is a slab with a flame cut into it.
Brush off the slab and press the flame
The slab sinks. The ground under the spire opens, and a bird of fire rises out of the dark, shaking off the dust.
claw marks in the ice
Deep claw marks score the ice here, all leading to one patch that is thinner than the rest.
Break through the thin ice
The thin ice gives way with a crack. The den floor shifts, and a great blue wolf climbs up out of the frozen dark.
a riddle carved in the floor
A riddle is carved into the floor stone, half worn away: “What has no door, yet opens for the patient?” A paw print is cut beside it.
Press the paw print
The floor stone slides away. Sand pours into the dark below, and a violet sphinx rises out of it with its eyes already open.
an old iron ring in the grass
Half hidden in the long grass is an old iron ring, rusted, set into a stone.
The ground shudders. The middle of the maze sinks and turns, and a great bull of orange armour rises up out of the earth.
